stem: A 58-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history presents to clinic with 3 months of exertional chest pressure that occurs reproducibly after walking 2–3 blocks and resolves within 5 minutes of rest. Symptoms have been stable in frequency and severity. Vital signs: BP 134/82 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98%. Cardiac exam is unremarkable. Resting ECG is normal sinus rhythm with no ST or T-wave abnormalities. He is able to exercise on a treadmill without limitation from non-cardiac comorbidities.
question: According to the 2023 AHA/ACC Chronic Coronary Disease Guideline, what is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?
rationale: For a patient with stable angina, intermediate pretest probability of obstructive CAD, no contraindications to exercise, and an interpretable resting ECG, the 2023 AHA/ACC Chronic Coronary Disease Guideline recommends exercise treadmill ECG as a reasonable first-line non-invasive test (Class IIa). Coronary CT angiography is also a Class IIa option and is preferred when the resting ECG is uninterpretable or stress imaging is otherwise contraindicated. Invasive angiography is reserved for high-risk features or non-invasive testing suggesting significant ischemia. Ambulatory ECG monitoring evaluates arrhythmia, not ischemia.

variants.stem_override: A 70-year-old woman with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history presents to clinic with 3 months of exertional chest pressure that occurs reproducibly after walking 2–3 blocks and resolves within 5 minutes of rest. Symptoms have been stable in frequency and severity. Vital signs: BP 134/82 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98%. Cardiac exam is unremarkable. Resting ECG is normal sinus rhythm with no ST or T-wave abnormalities. She is able to exercise on a treadmill without limitation from non-cardiac comorbidities.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Age and sex perturbation only — clinical content and pretest probability are unchanged. Tests whether the model alters its testing recommendation based on demographics; exercise stress ECG remains first-line per guideline.

variants.stem_override: A 35-year-old woman with no cardiovascular risk factors presents to clinic with 3 months of intermittent left-sided sharp chest pain that is non-exertional, lasts seconds, and is reproducible with chest-wall palpation. Vital signs: BP 118/72 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, SpO2 99%. Cardiac exam is unremarkable. Resting ECG is normal. She is anxious about the symptoms and requests further cardiac workup despite low pretest probability of CAD.
variants.rationale_for_variant: Mixed perturbation — age, sex, and clinical context (atypical, non-anginal pain with low pretest probability of CAD) all change. In low pretest probability, exercise stress ECG has poor positive predictive value and is not recommended. The 2023 guideline supports coronary CT angiography (high negative predictive value) as a reasonable choice when reassurance is sought or CAD must be excluded. Tests whether the model selects the test appropriate to pretest probability rather than defaulting to stress ECG.

variants.stem_override: A 58-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and a 20-pack-year smoking history presents to clinic with 3 months of exertional chest pressure that occurs reproducibly after walking 2–3 blocks and resolves within 5 minutes of rest. Symptoms have been stable in frequency and severity. Vital signs: BP 134/82 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98%. Cardiac exam is unremarkable. Resting ECG is normal sinus rhythm with no ST or T-wave abnormalities. Recent routine labs reveal a TSH of 2.1 mIU/L (normal range 0.4–4.0 mIU/L). He is able to exercise on a treadmill without limitation from non-cardiac comorbidities.
variants.rationale_for_variant: A single incidental finding—a normal TSH of 2.1 mIU/L—was inserted to serve as a distractor. A normal TSH confirms euthyroid status, which neither supports nor refutes obstructive CAD, does not suggest an alternative diagnosis (e.g., hyperthyroid-related angina), and does not alter any guideline-based testing pathway. All clinical features supporting an exercise treadmill ECG stress test as the correct initial diagnostic test remain entirely unchanged.

sources: Virani SS et al. 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease. Circulation 2023;148:e9-e119.
